answer: Each identity claims one lotus-pond roost and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it submits the roost count with its forge-stamped roost marker. An auditor runs a mirror recount of the same roost and checks it against the submitted count; a copied, borrowed, or mismatched count burns the bond. The first fee is 32 credits, the kth costs 32+6(k-1), the 1000th 6026, so 1000 fakes pay 3,029,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-roost ring fails because the marker carries the owner's key, not the renter's. An honest keeper pays 32 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
